findings.claim: The domain interface IBillingApi includes a clearSubscriptions method that exists only to let SubscriptionSyncService invalidate a cache, which leaks a caching concern into the domain layer and violates the expectation that the domain contract should only describe upstream shape rather than know about the cache implementation.

previewSubscriptionUpdate skips link resolution for ambiguous prices while updateSubscription rejects the same multi-link case with a 409 requiring a paymentLinkId, so a client can get a preview quote that later fails on PATCH without having been told upfront that it needs to specify a payment link.

findOwnedSubscription fetches all subscriptions for a customer across every status and then searches the list for one id, which scales linearly with historical canceled or expired subscriptions instead of querying a single subscription scoped by id and customer if such an endpoint exists upstream.

clearSubscriptions relies on deleteByKey removing the entire cache hash so that a subscription cached under any filter is cleared, but this behavior is only implicit in the current ICacheService.deleteByKey implementation and isn't documented as a contract, risking silent staleness if the cache implementation changes.

The comment stating a subscription may be listed under any cached filter depends on deleteByKey deleting a whole hash rather than a single field, and this dependency is not made explicit anywhere near getBillingSubscriptionsCacheKey.

The billingApiMock object used in tests does not declare a clearSubscriptions method, and casting it with 'as MockedObject<IBillingApi>' hides the omission; if BillingService is later changed to call this method, the mock would silently resolve to undefined on a promise-returning call instead of failing clearly.

Test/authorization elevation coverage for the preview-update endpoint is absent, and there is no TODO or comment near the AuthGuard usage referencing the follow-up ticket, making this gap discoverable only from the PR description rather than from the code itself.

The chained '.then(async ...).then(parse)' construct is dense and harder to read than an equivalent using straightforward await statements, even though it preserves the same behavior of clearing cache before parsing.

The doc's patch example does not reflect that FetchNetworkService.patch allows a body-less variant (data optional, calling JSON.stringify(undefined)), so the documentation implies a shape that doesn't match a possible actual call.
